structure.note: One class of common stock. Walton Enterprises, LLC, managed by four WELLCO Mgmt Trusts whose trustees are Walton family members, holds 3,002,673,393 shares and votes another 581,930,458 shares owned by the Walton Family Holdings Trust under an irrevocable proxy, for 44.80% in total. The proxy calls this 'approximately 45%' held by entities related to Sam Walton's family. That is below 50%, so the company is not majority-controlled on these figures.

notes: Fiscal year ended January 31, 2025 (Walmart calls it fiscal 2025; matches data.js fy 'Jan 2025'). Filings are the FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0000104169-25-000021) and the 2025 proxy statement (accession 0000104169-25-000055), as of April 11, 2025 with 8,000,886,911 Shares outstanding. All figures were re-read from those EDGAR documents on www.sec.gov on 2026-11-23 (replacing the pilot's stock.walmart.com PDF renderings); cash and stock-comp values are cross-checked against SEC XBRL. FAMILY HOLDING: the proxy lists Walton Enterprises, LLC at 44.80% and the Walton Family Holdings Trust at 7.27%, but the 44.80% already includes the trust's 581,930,458 shares (footnote 4: Walton Enterprises has sole voting power over them by irrevocable proxy). The trust is therefore not listed as a separate holder; adding it would double-count. Individual Walton family members' own holdings (e.g. directors Greg Penner and Steuart Walton in the officers-and-directors table) are not added, because the proxy does not give an aggregate for them and they may overlap with the family entities. VANGUARD: the 5.16% is stale. The proxy bases it solely on a Schedule 13G reporting ownership as of December 29, 2023, split-adjusted, while the percentage uses the April 11, 2025 share count. DIVIDENDS exclude $576 million paid to noncontrolling interest. STOCK COMP: the cash-flow statement has no separate share-based compensation line; the figure is the note total ($2,769 million, which the note also rounds to $2.8 billion), including plans of consolidated subsidiaries granted in their own stock.

supplierSpend.label: Spent with suppliers

taxesCollected.label: Taxes collected from customers and paid
taxesCollected.period: FYE 2026 (fiscal year ended Jan 31, 2026; newer than the FY2025 snapshot)

taxesPaid.label: Taxes paid directly by Walmart

taxesPaid.definition: "State and Local Taxes (including but not limited to: Income Tax, Property Tax, and Sales Tax) paid directly by Walmart to state and local tax jurisdictions in addition to the taxes collected and paid on behalf of customers for FYE 2026."

footprint.notes: U.S. state rows (50 states + DC) come from Walmart's corporate location-facts pages (corporate.walmart.com/about/location-facts/united-states/<state>). The pages render their numbers from a single company-hosted data file, locations.js, which is the document cited and quoted; the state pages themselves ship empty placeholders. The footnotes on the state pages date each measure differently and all but supplier spend are newer than the Jan 2025 snapshot: retail units as of Jan 19, 2026; associates and average wage as of Jul 25, 2025; taxes for FYE 2026; supplier spend FYE 2025 (Dun & Bradstreet). No archived FY2025 edition was used (archives are mirrors). Money values are published rounded ('$1.9 B', '$170.8 M', or exact dollars such as '$183,718' for Delaware and '$340,126' for Montana taxes collected) and are stored in USD millions; quotes carry a bracketed conversion where it changes the number. 'N/A' entries were omitted, not zeroed. totalRetailUnits is used as published, not summed from formats (Alabama's formats sum to 143 vs 144 published). averageWage uses a nonstandard unit (USD per hour) because no listed unit fits. The data file has copy errors in prose (Alaska's description mentions Texas) but stateID/state fields match every key and no two states share an identical stats block. Puerto Rico is also in the file (not a state; omitted from usStates and countries). Country rows are Walmart International unit counts from the Q4 FY2025 'Unit Counts and Square Footage' PDF on stock.walmart.com; the FY2025 10-K no longer prints a by-country table (Item 2 gives only segment totals: Walmart U.S. 4,605, Sam's Club U.S. 600, International 5,566). U.S. total units 5,205 are not repeated as a country row. Walmart's country location-facts pages give current (2026) unit totals only, no associates.
